Rural dialysis network: three and three.context: What is realistic for us: we could have started with up to 30 chairs instead of 20; new chairs cannot be built and installed in less than 3 months; we could review chair orders as often as monthly; we could order chairs for a target wait as short as three weeks instead of two months; and longer opening hours could get each chair to start at most 1.5 patients a month instead of 1.2.

Coffee-growing cooperative: three and th.policy: put 70% of the harvest income into new planting instead of half
Coffee-growing cooperative: three and th.context: What is realistic for us: cover crops, composting and resting plots could bring worn soil back in as little as 5 years instead of 15; we could put anywhere from a quarter to 70% of the harvest income into new planting (half now); paying for extra pickers could at most double the hectares a family can look after well, from 10 to 20; and shade trees and wider spacing could cut how fast cropping wears the soil by at most a third.

Kitchen fitting backlog: three and three.policy: push the crews harder when the backlog is high, so they can fit up to 1.7 times their normal pace instead of 1.4
Kitchen fitting backlog: three and three.context: What is realistic for us: we can let the crews rush to at most 1.7 times their normal pace, or not let them rush at all; a final check before sign-off could at best halve the snags on a normal job (about 1 in 10 now); we cannot find and train a fitter in under 20 weeks (about 30 now); we could have started with at most 13 crews instead of 11; and we cannot promise a fit sooner than 4 weeks after the order, because the units take that long to arrive, nor quote more than 8.

Regional electricians' guild: three and.policy: when work outgrows the guild, take on enough extra apprentices to close the gap within eighteen months instead of two years
Regional electricians' guild: three and.context: What is realistic for us: we could promise to keep taking on up to three apprentices a month however slow work gets (we have never set a minimum); we could close a gap between the electricians the work needs and those we have within as little as a year instead of two; and with encouragement up to four masters in five could supervise an apprentice instead of three in five.

Hospital contract cleaning standard: thr.policy: pay the cleaners for 10% overtime, so each works about 176 hours a month instead of 160
Hospital contract cleaning standard: thr.context: What is realistic for us: we could pay for overtime of up to 20%, so a cleaner works at most 192 hours a month instead of 160; recruiting and vetting could be sped up so a new cleaner starts in as little as 2 months instead of 4; the contractor could review how many cleaners it needs as often as every month instead of every three months; and the standard is the committee's to keep: it can stop lowering it, or lower it more slowly than now (it closes a miss over about a year), but there is no sense in lowering it faster.
